course.title: Web Application Programming and Hacking
course.description: This covers basic web application development with front-end (HTML5, JavaScript, CSS) and back-end (PHP/MySQL). Web application vulnerabilities and attacks will be introduced and explored with hands-on exercises on the range. Secure programming principles and practices will be introduced to avoid potential web application vulnerabilities and attacks.

labs.title: Lab 0
labs.text: This lab is covered in Lecture 2, with preparation homework in Lecture 1. In Part I, I setup an Ubuntu 22.04 Virtual Machine on VirtualBox and installed software and applications. In Part II, I cloned the course repository and my private repository and completed git exercises to write the report.

labs.title: Lab 1
labs.text: This lab is covered in Lecture 3 with the following parts. For Lab 1 there were two parts. Part I has two tasks. The first is getting familiar with Wireshark and the use of the HTTP protocol within this tool. For this task I downloaded Wireshark through the terminal and started capturing packets. For task 2, I sent a minimal HTTP Request with telnet and captured packets with Wireshark to inspect the Request and Response parameters of HTTP. Part II had three tasks. The first task involved developing and deploying CGI Web applications in C with the deployment itself being through the browser. For task 2, I developed and deployed PHP pages by using a simple string and global variable to display my name. For task 3, I used Wireshark to inspect HTTP GET and HTTP POST Requests and Responses. With those packets I could see major differences between the two.

labs.title: Lab 2
labs.text: This lab consisted of multiple hands-on exercises covered in Lectures 4-6. For Lab 2 there were two tasks. Task 1 has two parts. Part a was creating webpages with the basic HTML tags. The webpage implemented used basic HTML tags with forms and an adjusted image. For Part b, I used simple JavaScript code within the HTML file to implement and show the Date and Email when clicked by the user. And a digital and analog clock was also integrated into the webpage. Task 2 has four parts. Part a was implementing Ajax GET requests and keypress logging. Part b was implementing CSS with a class in JavaScript. There are three types of CSS implementation (inline, internal, external). For Part c, I implemented jQuery Ajax GET and POST requests to echo.php using the existing class for the button and adding functions for each request. For Part d, I integrated Web APIs with Ajax and fetch().

labs.title: Hackathon 1
labs.text: This hackathon consisted of multiple hands-on exercises covered in Lectures 7-8, where I performed cross-site scripting attacks on multiple levels to understand the vulnerabilities as well as defense methods. For Hackathon 1, there were two tasks. Task 1 focused on cross-site scripting attacks at increasing levels of difficulty. They required injecting code to get an alert(). Task 2 focused on the implementation of input validation and XSS defense methods in previous Labs 1 and 2.

labs.title: Individual Project 1
labs.text: In this project, I expanded my front-end web development skills by developing a Professional Profile Website and deploying it on the github.io cloud service.
